comment: Bona fide registry of the agent-CLI harnesses, model providers, and their bindings. This file is DATA, not code: adding a harness or model is adding an entry here (a harness entry is only usable once a driver with the same id exists in packages/eval/src/harness). Model metadata (vendor, release, context, per-token price, effort levels, vision) is enriched from the models.dev catalog snapshot that OpenCode caches (~/.cache/opencode/models.json); price_band derives from the output $/Mtok. v2 adds three orthogonal axes — provider (canonical entity that serves/bills), credential_route (how the call is authed/billed), and wire protocols — plus attribution and probe metadata verified live on 2026-07-23. 'Adapter required' is DERIVED (provider protocols ∩ harness protocols = ∅), never stored per pair. Unknown metadata is null; the console renders null as unknown, never as zero.

probe_policy.token_strategy: unique random token per run, written to a file in an otherwise-empty fixture dir — asserting the token proves TOOL USE (a real file read), not model recall
rules: SERIALIZE probe runs: overlapping probes produced false 240s timeouts (codex, opencode) on 2026-07-23
Per-harness timeout_ms is mandatory: observed latency spread is ~9-17x (pi 2.2s .. codex 38.7s)
Re-probe after any install/update event; honor warmup_after_install (opencode's first post-install run failed transiently)
capability and attribution are INDEPENDENT assertions: a binding that runs but routes to the wrong provider fails differently (attribution_mismatch) than one that does not run (fail_capability)
attribution observed_by_driver=false can never yield a full 'pass' — cap at pass_provider_unverified

version.note: On the git route `--version` is NOT a build identifier: the semver only changes at release commits (874 commits all reported 0.19.0), and its 'upstream <sha>' names the remote tip, not the installed commit. One release carries dual ids (GitHub date tag v2026.7.20 == PyPI 0.19.0). Identity = `git -C ~/.hermes/hermes-agent rev-parse HEAD`.
